entities.summary:
Arnold II of Horne (arnold-ii-of-horne) was a prominent figure in the 14th-century European religious landscape. He served as the Prince and Bishop of Liège (Liège, Flanders) from 1378 until his death in 1389, leaving a lasting legacy in the governance of the region. During his tenure, he oversaw the implementation of various reforms aimed at strengthening the Catholic Church's presence in the area.

As a key player in the complex web of alliances and rivalries between European kingdoms, Arnold II of Horne played a crucial role in shaping the regional dynamics of the time. His diplomatic efforts and strategic marriages helped secure the interests of the Bishopric of Liège, while also contributing to the growth of the Catholic Church's influence in the region.

Arnold II of Horne's impact on the historical record is evident in the numerous accounts of his life and reign, which provide valuable insights into the politics, culture, and society of 14th-century Europe. His legacy can be seen in the continued importance of the Bishopric of Liège as a center of Catholic worship and governance.

The sheer breadth of Arnold II of Horne's accomplishments is a testament to his enduring influence on the course of European history. His remarkable story serves as a poignant reminder of the complex interplay between politics, religion, and culture that defined the medieval era.
